questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘incarcerate’.

questions.question: Which tense is used for an action that started in the past and continues to the present and possibly into the future?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Present Perfect tense is widely used to talk about an action or actions that started in the past and continues in the present, and might extend into the future.
 
• It is formed with the present tense of "to have" (have/has) and the past participle of the verb.
 
• Neither Future Perfect, Past Continuous, nor Future Continuous tenses can express an action that begins in the past and extends to the present (or future).

**Therefore, the correct answer is- 'Present Perfect tense'.**

• The Future Perfect tense (Option B) refers to a completed action in the future.
 
• The Past Continuous tense (Option C) refers to a specific time in the past when an ongoing action was interrupted by another event.
 
• The Future Continuous tense (Option D) indicates that an action will be ongoing at a certain time in the future

__
 
• The present perfect continuous tense is used to describe actions that started in the past and are still continuing in the present.
 
• The correct structure for the present perfect continuous tense is: **Subject + has/have been + verb (ing) + additional details.**
 
• In the sentence **"She has been living in this city for five years,"** the action of living started in the past and continues in the present.

• **Question:** Have they been playing football since morning?
